page.overview:
Who is Ravi Sengir?

Ravi, now better known as Grandmother Ravi Sengir, is a former planeswalker and the adopted grandmother of Baron Sengir, on Ulgrotha. During the New Phyrexia's Invasion of the Multiverse she defended Ulgrotha.

Ravi grew up as a farmer girl with her parents, in a village in the shadow of the local baron's castle. At one point, the village became infested with Plague Rats, causing the death of almost all the inhabitants, Ravi's mother among them. At her funeral, the girl met a strange boy, richly dressed. He revealed that he was the baron's son and that the baron was studying black magic: not only didn't he care about the villagers, but it was he who had brought the rats. The boy told Ravi that the baron wanted to become immortal, and had started doing strange things to his son, like making him sleep in a coffin. The only way to free the village from the rats continued the boy, was to kill the baron. However, the law prohibited a son who killed his father to inherit, so only Ravi could kill the baron. To do this, the boy taught her a song that could control the rats.

Ravi, however, didn't want to kill a man, even one as cruel as the baron. She changed her mind about this when her father also passed away due to the infestation. Ravi saw almost all of the village empty, and without any other relatives and with nowhere to go, she decided she would do as the boy had suggested. Singing the song, she controlled the rats in a way that impressed the boy, since only a powerful wizard could sing and dominate the rats so well. That night, the two entered the baron's castle and reached the lord's sanctum, the charmed swarm of rats following them. Once again, Ravi faltered in her resolve to kill a man in cold blood, but when she realized that the baron was working on her mother's corpse, she lost every hesitation and commanded the rats to devour him. The baron was a mighty wizard too, and managed to repel the rats with the same song. Confused by the battle of wills, the rats attacked the only other prey in the room: the boy. When the baron saw his son dead, he cast a spell on him, interrupting the song. Ravi took her opportunity and ordered the rats to kill the baron. After the deed, she commanded the rats to leave the village forever. Exhausted, Ravi opened one of the closed windows to breathe fresh air and bask in the rising sunlight. A scream behind her made her turn around: the boy was still alive, brought back to life by the last spell cast by his father, but he was seemingly intolerant to light. The boy noted how Ravi must have been a powerful wizard for having overpowered the baron and he believed she would become a planeswalker. The girl, however, doesn't seem to be interested in magic. The two realized that they didn't know each other's name: Ravi was thus introduced to the new Baron Sengir. Unbeknownst to both of them, they would be reunited many centuries later.
